clue.text: Underwear line made smaller for French establishment

indicators.note: cutting the last letter off makes the line one letter shorter

blocks.note: SERIES (a line of things) minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A lingerie brand shrinks its range to suit a French shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a clothing range being cut back; in fact 'line' is SERIES, which loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French restaurant, an establishment in France.

clue.text: Overdo it grabbing empty bottles

clue.text: Circus attraction features teams in what way?

blocks.note: sides are teams in a match

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a circus act manages to include whole teams.

clue.text: Flier showcasing reduced clothing

explanation.walkthrough: Robing is a noun for clothing, especially ceremonial robes; dropping the G leaves the bird.

clue.text: Former taxi company worker, for one, is high-spirited

blocks.note: a worker ant is one kind of ant

clue.text: Thief to make decision in pool?

explanation.walkthrough: Pool here is the cue game, not a swimming pool; the question mark flags the playful second reading as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket is a thief who steals from people's pockets.

clue.text: Flavour for some scotch eggs originally found in bit of butter

clue.text: Majority of gel pens in medical centre

clue.text: Plot to succeed — leave carrying large bed cover

clue.text: Freedom to transport English character in A Streetcar Named Desire

blocks.clueFragment: character in A Streetcar Named Desire

clue.text: Proceeded with punishment from coach, entering river backwards

the river's name is read in reverse

running laps is a coach's punishment

clue.text: Character running to catch one creature in the north

clue.text: Went back with Frenchman, eg to return diamonds

clue.text: Like some architecture in British university town’s entrance — top-tier

blocks.note: A-list = top tier, as of celebrities

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a grand college gate; 'entrance' simply means the first letter.

clue.text: Get to give a sermon without introduction

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to' looks like 'be allowed to', but it means arrive at.

clue.text: Hotel gets irritated about entourage

blocks.note: H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet
the surface verb, read as ANGERS
on = about, as in 'a book on birds'

explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container instruction, but it is ON, as in 'a talk on something'.

clue.text: Crème de la crème of joints to the east of Brentford FC

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joints' suggests roasts or pubs, but they are body joints. Brentford FC is a London football club whose nickname is The Bees.

clue.text: Busy period in pirates’ domain, with no going back

indicators.note: going back means travelling in reverse, so the word is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Pirates have a busy time, with no chance of retreating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no going back' sounds like an irreversible commitment; it tells you to reverse NO.
explanation.definitionFit: High season is the busiest time of year, especially for tourism.

clue.text: Small vegetable established to be the most shiny

blocks.note: est. = established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A little vegetable is proved to be the glossiest.
explanation.walkthrough: EST is the abbreviation seen on signs like 'Est. 1850'.

clue.text: Policeman, one stopping pot user — an artist

indicators.note: plugs a gap in the other word, sitting inside it

clue.text: Generally, popular home occupied by those people first of all?

the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A popular home is taken over by certain people, it seems, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular home' reads as a well-liked house, but it is two short words side by side, pulled apart so that the people and the letter from 'all' can move in between.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main means generally or for the most part.

clue.text: You and I must be seen in fancy theatres, darling

indicators.note: WE has to appear inside the other letters
made elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple insist on being spotted at glamorous theatres, dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy theatres' reads as grand venues, but 'fancy' is an order to rearrange; the couple then slot in after the first letter.

clue.text: Wow — fib about extremely dashing old leader

the extremes of the word, its outer letters

explanation.surface: Amazing: a lie about a very dashing former leader.
explanation.walkthrough: COO then LI(DG)E. 'Extremely dashing' looks like praise for the leader but asks for the ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Calvin Coolidge was US president from 1923 to 1929, so a leader from long ago.

clue.text: Violently liberates northern walled city once

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone forcibly frees a northern city that used to be walled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nearly tells the history: the Berlin Wall fell in 1989, freeing the city's east.
explanation.definitionFit: East Berlin was the half of the city enclosed by the Berlin Wall until 1989.

clue.text: Certify central portion of data examination

clue.text: Footballer with a bit of money getting on with support

clue.text: Improperly, mainly invest in island

most of the word, dropping its last letter

clue.text: Breach metal around front of opening underneath instrument

the first letter of the word
